record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.original_question: For a fixed affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how large is the family of trivialising vector fields X=X(γ) associated with graph cocycles γ∈ker d? Is the vector space of these vector fields locally complete enough to approximate arbitrary vector fields on the manifold, so that the exponentials of the trivialising fields could effectively imitate a smooth structure on the affine Poisson manifold?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. In the above setting, how ample is the set of trivialising vector fields X = X(γ ∈ ker d) ∈ Γ(TM^r_aff) on a given manifold (M^r_aff,P) with a fixed Poisson structure ? Is the vector space of these fields X locally complete, to be sufficient for the approximation of arbitrary vector fields on M^r_aff ? In brief, are the exponents of the trivialising vector fields X(γ,P) enough to imitate a smooth structure on an affine Poisson manifold ?

artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph cocycles and Poisson geometry
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ be an affine Poisson manifold of dimension $r$, that is, a smooth manifold equipped with a Poisson bivector $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$ whose components in some affine atlas are polynomial (in particular, take the standard affine setting in which $P$ is given globally by polynomial coefficients). Consider the Kontsevich graph complex of unoriented finite graphs with a wedge-ordering on edges, equipped with the differential $d$ obtained by vertex-expansion. To each cocycle $\gamma\in\ker d$ one associates, via the Kontsevich orientation morphism applied to $(\gamma,P)$, a vector field $X(\gamma)=X(\gamma,P)\in\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$ — called a trivialising vector field — with the property that the bivector flow $\dot P=[\![P,X(\gamma)]\!]$ realises the infinitesimal Poisson-cohomology-trivial deformation produced by $\gamma$.
\medskip

Question. Describe the size of the family
$$\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)=\{\,X(\gamma,P): \gamma\in\ker d\,\}\subset\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}}).$$
More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Is the linear span of $\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$ locally complete in $\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$, in the sense that for every point $x\in M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$, every smooth vector field on a neighbourhood of $x$ can be approximated (in the $C^\infty$ topology) by elements of this span?
\item Equivalently, do the time-one flows $\exp(tX(\gamma,P))$, as $\gamma$ ranges over $\ker d$ and $t$ over $\mathbb{R}$, generate a (pseudo)group rich enough to imitate the full diffeomorphism action on $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ preserving $P$?
\end{enumerate}
Determine, for a given $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$, whether such local completeness holds, and if not, characterise the closure of $\mathrm{span}\,\mathcal{X}(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$ inside $\Gamma(TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question concerning the size and local completeness of the family of trivialising vector fields produced by Kontsevich graph cocycles on affine Poisson manifolds. No published resolution was located; the question appears to remain open.
